## Welcome to eRules Online Rule Filing

* * *

Before getting started, you must first create a Universal Access Account.

Access will be given when a completed original paper copy of the Electronic Filing of Rules Authorization Form (ERF) is submitted to the Secretary of State's Office.

The exact title number and rule(s) you have the ability to change or add must be listed on the form. If access to all of an agency's rules is being given, simply write "all" in the series number space on the form.

Once your account setup is complete you can use your login credentials to access the online eRules Filing application via the eRules Online Rule Filing Login page.

When working on rule filings it's important to remember:

  * All rule documents must be submitted in Word.
  * Supporting, adopted by reference, other, and comments received documents can be submitted in PDF.
  * Rules containing Track Changes, Markup, or Redline will not be accepted.
  * Each document uploaded in the eRules system must be submitted separately.
  * If there are personnel changes in your Agency requiring changes to permissions in the eRules system, please notify the Administrative Law Division.

## 2026–2027 Deadlines

* * *

  * July 1, 2026 is the last day to file a rule for the public comment period.
  * July 31, 2026 is the last day to file an Agency Approved rule.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Rule-Making Deadlines

* * *

Rule-making deadlines for the 2026 Legislative session are:

  * Wednesday, July 1, 2026 to put a rule out for public comment; and
  * Friday, July 31, 2026 to file an Agency Approved rule.

Legislative-Exempt, Interpretive and Procedural rules are not affected by deadlines and can be filed at any time during the year.

Deadlines for filing Legislative rules are found in W. Va. Code §29A-3-12(a). It establishes the deadline date for filing an Agency Approved rule with the Legislative Rule-Making Review Committee for consideration during the next Legislative session as the last Friday in July. Beginning in 2020, and every four years after, it is the last Friday in August. For rules filed with the Legislative Oversight Commission on Education Accountability, the deadline date is established by W. Va. Code §29A-3A-13.

## City Charters, Amendments, and Ordinances

* * *

During the 2026 Legislative session the state repository for city charters, amendments, and ordinances was transferred to the Secretary of State. The legislation directs cities to file related documents with the Secretary of State who shall preserve them as an authentic public record. Please see the City Charters Index for more information.

## Executive Records

* * *

Documents representing official acts of the Governor are entered into the Executive Journal. Executive Orders, Proclamations, and Appointments of State Officials are some of the records maintained.

In addition, the Executive Records section has also taken on the role of repository of certain other legal documents as a result of specific legislation.

To view documents available online, use the Executive Journal Search.

## State Register Portal

* * *

As traditional workspace and functionality needs have changed over the last few years, the Secretary of State's office has been addressing these needs and providing useful solutions. The Register Portal was created as an efficient document delivery system for State agencies that are required to publish non-rule documents in the State Register.

# Rule-Making Steps and Time Frame for Legislative Rules

It can take almost one (1) year for a legislative rule to complete the entire rule-making process. If changes to the W. Va. Code are needed, they must be made before the rule can be proposed. This could extend the time frame to two (2) years.

Please Note

See the Regulatory Moratorium to verify compliance.

All needed forms become available in the Secretary of State's eRules system when the rule is uploaded to the correct field.

## Legislative Rule-Making Steps

### Step 1

Public Comment Period

  * The agency makes the proposed rule available to the public for a written comment period, public hearing or both by filing a Notice of Public Comment Period with the Secretary of State's office.
  * The comment period must be for a minimum of thirty (30) days but not more than sixty (60) days.
  * The entire rule must be filed with language to be deleted struck-through and new language to be added underlined.
  * The form filed with the rule will contain the required information including the date, time and place for the receipt of public comments and/or hearing information.
  * Any "adopted by reference", "supporting documents", "other" documents and any tables, charts, diagrams etc. should be filed at this time for consideration throughout the rule-making process.

### Step 2

Agency Approved Filing

  * No later than ninety (90) days after the close of the comment period and after considering the comments received, the agency approves the rule for filing with LRMRC (Legislative Rule Making Review Committee) by filing a Notice of Agency Approval of a Proposed Rule with the Secretary of State's office.
  * The entire rule must be filed including any changes based on comments.
  * The form filed with the rule will contain the required information.
  * A copy of all comments received and/or a hearing transcript must be submitted.
  * The agency response to each comment must be submitted. An agency may consolidate substantially similar comments and responses in the interest of efficiency.

### Step 3

Modified Filing

  * LRMRC (Legislative Rule Making Review Committee) will meet and consider the proposed rules. If the committee approves the rule as filed, there are no more requirements until after the Legislative session. If the committee recommends changes, the agency files a Notice of Rule Modification with the Secretary of State's office.
  * The entire rule must be filed including the recommendations of LRMRC (Legislative Rule Making Review Committee).
  * The form filed with the rule will contain the required information.
  * The filing should be within ten (10) days of the date of the LRMRC (Legislative Rule Making Review Committee) meeting unless otherwise specified.

### Step 4

Waiting

  * All the proposed legislative rules are placed in bills and considered by the Legislature during session.
  * The Legislature may amend rules on the floor.
  * After the bill granting legislative approval for the promulgation of the rule is passed it is sent to the Governor for signature.

### Step 5

Final Filing

  * Upon passage of the bill and signature of the Governor, the agency files a Notice of Final Filing with the Secretary of State's office. This filing must be done within sixty (60) days of the effective date of the bill.
  * A clean copy of the entire rule must be filed including the removal of all strike-throughs and underlines and any changes made by the Legislature. The filing date, effective date and sunset date (if applicable) will be added to the General section of the rule.
  * The form filed with the rule will contain the required information.
  * The rule will become effective upon the final filing of the rule, or the date fixed by the authorizing act, or a date not to exceed ninety (90) days as fixed by the agency.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Rule-Making Steps and Time Frame for Legislative-Exempt, Procedural and Interpretive Rules

Legislative-exempt, procedural and interpretive rules can be in effect as soon as sixty (60) days after an agency proposes a rule.

Please Note

All needed forms become available in the Secretary of State's eRules system when the rule is uploaded to the correct field.

## Legislative-Exempt, Procedural and Interpretive Rule-Making Steps

### Step 1

Public Comment Period

  * The agency makes the proposed rule available to the public for a written comment period, public hearing or both by filing a Notice of Public Comment Period with the Secretary of State's office.
  * The comment period must be for a minimum of thirty (30) days but not more than sixty (60) days.
  * The entire rule must be filed with language to be deleted struck-through and new language to be added underlined.
  * The form filed with the rule will contain the required information including the date, time and place for the receipt of public comments and/or hearing information.
  * Any "adopted by reference", "supporting documents", "other" documents and any tables, charts, diagrams etc. must be filed at this time for consideration throughout the rule-making process.

### Step 2

Final Filing

  * After the close of the public comment period and after considering the comments received, the agency final files the rule.
  * A clean copy of the entire rule must be filed including the removal of all strike-throughs and underlines and any changes based on comments. The filing date and effective date will also be added to the General section of the rule.
  * A copy of all comments received and/or a hearing transcript along with the agency response to each comment, including any changes made, must be submitted. An agency may consolidate substantially similar comments and responses in the interest of efficiency.
  * The form filed with the rule will contain the required information including the effective date of the rule which must be at least thirty (30) days after the final filing and not later than sixty (60) days.

Remember

The agency must adopt or withdraw the rule within six (6) months after the close of the public comment period.

Failure to do so constitutes withdrawal.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Rules out for Public Comment

When an agency proposes a new rule or amends an existing rule, it must be made available to the public for written comments, public hearing or both.

All comments go directly to the Agency proposing the rule.

Detailed information is available on the form filed with the rule.

## Agency Approved Rules

After the comment period is closed, the agency may modify the proposed rule based on the comments received.

The rule is filed with the Legislative Rule Making Review Committee (LRMRC (Legislative Rule Making Review Committee)) or the Legislative Oversight Commission on Education Accountability (LOCEA (Legislative Oversight Commission on Education Accountability)) along with copies of the comments and the agency's response to them.

If LRMRC (Legislative Rule Making Review Committee) or LOCEA (Legislative Oversight Commission on Education Accountability) recommends no changes to the rule, this is the version that will be presented during the Legislative session.

## Modified Rules

When LRMRC (Legislative Rule Making Review Committee) or LOCEA (Legislative Oversight Commission on Education Accountability) recommends changes to the rule, the agency makes them and files it again as a Modified Rule.

This becomes the version that will be presented during the Legislative session.

## Emergency Rules

When a legislative rule is needed before it can complete the normal rule-making process and all statutory requirements are met, an emergency filing can be made.

Emergency is not a stand-alone rule type. It is a condition of a legislative rule that allows the needed changes to be in effect while going through the rule-making process.

An Emergency Rule can remain valid for up to 15 months or until the legislative rule becomes effective.

# West Virginia State Register

Search the Register to view the full text of the current and historical issues of the West Virginia Register.

The West Virginia Register is the title of a weekly online publication which gives the public quick access to current information about the status of rules moving through the rule-making process in addition to newly filed orders, decisions, opinions and actions of state entities.

The West Virginia Register is published online every Friday, with few exceptions. In weeks that end in a state holiday it is published on the last business day of that week.

The Register is a quick reference of filings, documents and notices received by the Administrative Law Division during the work week. Its purpose is to allow citizens to keep up-to-date on rule making and other official actions of state government agencies, boards and commissions.

The Register also contains the Rule Monitor, which is a table of all rules currently going through the process of being promulgated. With one quick glance, the Rule Monitor shows you the current status of a proposed rule and if anything new has been filed.

## About the Register

  * Background
  * Organization, Publication and Contents
  * Sections
  * Publication Deadlines

### Organization, Publication and Contents

Each year, a new volume begins with Volume Number and Issue 1. As additional issues are published on the last business day of each week, the Issue Number increases.

Search Tip: When searching Historical Registers, use the "Select Year" dropdown in the upper left corner of the Registers Results table to limit your search results to the year you select.

For each year, the date issued, volume number and issue number will be displayed.

Over the years, the State Register has been expanded to make more information conveniently available. We are continually working to find better ways to structure our information to make it easier to locate and utilize.

### Sections

Recent State Registers include the following sections:

Chronological Index

A listing of rules that have been put out for public comment or filed as an emergency during the week. It also provides information about where to send public comments and the deadline for receiving them.

Rule Monitor

Contains detailed information on the status of each proposed and emergency rule through the full rule-making process from the first filing until the date it goes into effect.

Orders Report

The orders report lists determination of fact or judgment tendered by an agency.

Official Filings

Different official filings required for legal action or other purpose including:

  * Executive Orders issued by the Governor
  * Attorney General Opinions
  * Ethics Commission Opinion
  * Tax Appeal Decisions
  * Grievance Decisions

Other Documents or Information Filed

This section includes notice of anything filed which does not fit within any of the other categories. The Administrative Procedures Act (APA) provides for these miscellaneous filings, and other sections of the Code sometimes require an agency to file a specific report or other document with the Secretary of State.

### Publication Deadlines

The Register publication date is the last business day of the week, ordinarily Friday, unless it has to be moved forward due to a holiday.

Filing closes at 5:00 p.m. the day before publication.

### Background

In 1982, the West Virginia Legislature established the "State Register" as the repository of all required filings listed in West Virginia Code §29A-2-3.

Originally, the term covered the full text of everything filed — rules, notices, orders, decisions, etc. — in addition to a rule monitor, cross index and chronological index. In order to meet these requirements and provide better service to the public, the Secretary of State reorganized the publication process in 1985.

So began the current practice of publishing, online, the weekly State Register containing weekly status updates as well as maintaining the full text of all rules filed in the Code of State Rules.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
